notes: §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.3 SRL3.3 has three sentences. (a) "When a figurative constant other than ALL literal is used, the word ALL is redundant and is used for readability only." The grammar rule figurativeConstant reads ALL before each of the five word classes and before a symbolic-character as an optional prefix; FigurativeOperand binds ALL ZEROS, ALL SPACE, ALL HIGH-VALUE, ALL LOW-VALUE and ALL QUOTE to the same BoundFigurative as the bare word, and Classify does the same for a VALUE clause and a level 88. The one place a later edition makes the word count, a numeric-only literal, is gated by GateAllZeroAsNumeric, silent at 85. The statements that refuse the ALL form at 85 do so under their own 1985 rules (§1985:VI.6.25.3 SR1 for STRING, §1985:VI.6.27.3 SR1 for UNSTRING, §1985:VI.6.18.3 SR3 for INSPECT). (b) "the actual characters associated with each figurative constant depend upon the program collating sequence specified", "Except in the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph": FillChar takes the high and low characters of the PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE alphabet, which Extremes computes with the tie rules of §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR5 and GR6, and a figurative constant written in an ALPHABET or CLASS clause is read by SpecialNamesFigurative through AlphabetFigurative, which gives the native extremes (§1985:VI.4.5.4 GR7). No arm is edition-keyed. (c) "the constructs using the word ALL, such as ALL literal, ALL SPACES, etc., which are composed of two distinct character-strings": ALL and the word are two lexer tokens, each figurative word one token. Probed at --std 85: with and without ALL the five words and a symbolic-character give the same result in MOVE (alphanumeric, numeric, numeric edited, group, reference-modified receivers), VALUE on elementary and group items, level 88, IF, EVALUATE, PERFORM UNTIL, INITIALIZE REPLACING and DISPLAY (one character); ALL and ZEROS on separate lines with a comment line and a blank line between, or separated by a comma, are read as the one constant. Under PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE over an alphabet whose first character is "B" and last is "A", HIGH-VALUE is A and LOW-VALUE is B in MOVE, VALUE, a relation, a level 88 and SET TO TRUE, DISPLAY, STRING, UNSTRING, INSPECT, SEARCH, INITIALIZE and a contained program, while CLASS ... IS LOW-VALUE THRU "9" and CLASS ... IS HIGH-VALUE keep the native characters. An alphabet that leaves native characters unnamed has the last of them (U+FFFF, the implementor's 65,536-character native set) as its highest, so HIGH-VALUE is that character there. The witness moves ALL ZEROS and ZEROS to two PIC X(3) items and displays SAME and 000.

next.reason: 1985: 'the word ALL is redundant and is used for readability only', so with SRL3.1 ('the only figurative constant permitted is ZERO') ALL ZERO stood wherever ZERO did, a numeric-only literal included. 2023 drops the redundancy statement and §2023:8.3.3.6.3 SR1 a) permits there only 'ZERO (ZEROS, ZEROES) without the ALL phrase': ALL ZERO in that position, accepted in 1985, is refused (a case removed), so CHANGED. Kept parts: ALL optional in formats 1-5 (FMT-8.3.3.6.2) with one character when 'other than ALL literal-1' (§2023:8.3.3.6.4 GR3); HIGH/LOW-VALUE follow the program collating sequence except in SPECIAL-NAMES (§2023:12.3.7.4 GR8, GR9; §2023:8.3.3.6.4 GR6, GR7).
